slides.title:
They *felt* faster.
They were ==slower.==
slides.sub: A controlled trial: 16 experienced devs, 246 real tasks
slides.source: Source: METR, "Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity" (July 2025)
slides.alt: Column chart from the METR randomized trial with 16 experienced open-source developers and 246 tasks. Developers expected AI to make them 24% faster and felt 20% faster afterwards, but measured completion time was 19% slower, shown as a red bar below the zero line.

slides.title: Why the *slowdown*?
slides.sub: What the developers in the trial reported:

items.title: They knew the code better than the AI
items.text: Least help on issues they were most familiar with

items.title: Large, complex repos
items.text: Mature projects with 1M+ lines and strict standards

items.title: Prompt, wait, review, fix
items.text: Time saved writing was spent checking output

slides.takeaway: A snapshot of early-2025 tools in one setting, not proof that AI slows everyone down.
slides.alt: Three reasons for the slowdown reported in the METR trial: developers knew the code better than the AI, the repositories were large and complex, and time saved writing code was spent prompting, waiting and reviewing output. Caveat: a snapshot of early-2025 tools in one setting, not proof that AI slows everyone.

post.caption:
84% of developers are adopting AI coding tools, but only 33% trust what those tools write.

The Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 (49,000+ devs) found that more developers now distrust AI accuracy (46%) than trust it. The #1 frustration: AI code that's "almost right, but not quite" (66%).

Then there's METR's controlled trial. Experienced open-source developers expected AI to make them 24% faster and felt 20% faster afterwards. Measured on 246 real tasks, they were 19% slower. It's a small study of early-2025 tools, but the gap between how fast AI feels and how fast it actually is should worry anyone who has stopped checking.

Slide 7 has 5 habits that close that gap. Save it for your next AI-assisted PR.

Honest answer in the comments: has AI made you FASTER, SLOWER or the SAME?
